To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the slip length formulae of Crowdy (2016) for flow in a superhydrophobic channel with protruding menisci and longitudinal ridges are valid over a wide range of parameters and that the slip length is not affected by the protruding meniscus touching the opposing wall.

(i) the slip length formulae derived here for flow in channels with superhydrophobic surfaces are accurate even for ridge period as large as 20% of the channel width, and (ii) the slip length of a channel with one superhydrophobic wall is approximately half that of a channel with both walls superhydrophobic.

the asymptotic slip length formulae for flow past a single ridge are valid over a wide range of ridge periods, even those where the menisci protrude far enough into the air to touch the opposite wall; and, the asymptotic formulae can be applied to a wide range of protrusion heights, even those that are so large that the menisci are touching the opposite wall.
